source_anchor: CI-1 — Fail-silent gate: absence, error, or a not-quite-matching predicate reads as pass
instance: A QA gate's condition tested `ran_ok===false` instead of `!==true` in creation-loop.js, and separately a `hashFiles()` call inside a job-level `if:` made a GH Actions workflow unparseable so it never appeared in `gh pr checks` at all — both cases read as pass when the check never truly ran or errored.
check: Assert the expected check row is present in results (not just non-red); require every failure path to return nonzero matching structured status; a gate's condition should enumerate the success set, never test absence of one failure value.

source_anchor: CI-2 — URL/identity trust by substring instead of parsing the host
instance: A URL/host trust check matched a trusted substring anywhere in the string, so `https://evil.example/github.com/owner/x` (substring in path) and `https://github.com@evil.com/...` (in userinfo) both passed as trusted (PR #19).
check: Strip scheme, then userinfo, isolate host (strip port), require exact string equality against the trusted value; read the raw configured value, not a rewritten one.

source_anchor: CI-3 — Tests encode the author's blind spot (happy-path-only)
instance: A green test suite written by the same author/agent as the fix never covered the exact edge case an independent adversarial reviewer with a PoC found (PRs #19/#20).
check: Require an independent adversarial reviewer with a PoC before trusting a self-authored green suite; every fix ships at least one test written to defeat it, not confirm it.

source_anchor: CI-4 — Silent semantic broadening when editing a predicate
instance: Flipping a predicate from `== "SUCCESS"` to `!= "SUCCESS"` in `evaluate_checks` (PR #20) silently began matching/dropping values like NEUTRAL/SKIPPED that nobody had enumerated, and docs still described the old value set.
check: Enumerate every value newly included/excluded when touching a filter predicate; use explicit allow/deny sets, never 'anything != X'; update docs in the same change.

source_anchor: CI-5 — Trusting untrusted control input
instance: A `run`/`cwd` field read from checked-in repo config, a harness-writable `meta.json` naming a branch to delete, and an unauthenticated PR comment's `VERDICT:` keyword were each treated as operator-issued control input (cli-dispatch #13/#17/#11).
check: Establish provenance/origin ownership before trusting executable config; cross-check against an authoritative source (git worktree list --porcelain); verify commenter identity via authorAssociation/allowlist, not just keyword presence.

source_anchor: CI-6 — Coordinator prescribes fix as a type-list instead of a semantic rule
instance: A coordinator's fix instruction named the affected types instead of the semantic invariant, so the implementer generalized the mechanism (not the reasoning) to a type the invariant never applied to and broke a case the brief never meant to touch (engram-go PR #1405, round 1→2).
check: Reviewer asks 'why does each listed type belong?' before accepting a type-list as fix scope; briefs must state the semantic invariant, never a bare type enumeration.

source_anchor: CI-7 — Batch-boundary blind spot
instance: A dedup/data-loss fix verified correct call-to-call was only retested at the old per-call cardinality; a concurrent, seemingly unrelated batching change in the same PR raised per-call cardinality through the same chokepoint and reintroduced the original bug in-batch (engram-go PR #1405, round 2→3).
check: When a change raises how many items flow through an existing chokepoint per call, re-test that chokepoint's assumptions at the new cardinality, not just the old one.

source_anchor: CI-8 — A validation canary that tests a correlated property instead of the guarded property
instance: A corruption-detection canary tested a correlated but different property (arithmetic ability), so a healthy 0.5B model too small for arithmetic failed the canary for a reason unrelated to corruption; a reasoning model separately failed by being pushed past its token window.
check: A gate must test the exact property it guards; for corruption detection, assert non-degenerate output (non-empty, not all-one-token, no repeated garbage) — never a capability task the subject might legitimately fail.

source_anchor: CI-9 — A "known-good" fixture is not a validation oracle
instance: Zero findings on a 'known-good' fixture was treated as proof the discovery loop was correct, but real attackers found a genuine bug in that fixture (NaN defeats a lo>hi clamp guard since every NaN comparison is False).
check: The oracle for a discovery loop is termination behavior (goes dry, bounded, ranks correctly), never a specific finding count; any finding on a 'clean' fixture is a real bug or a verifier-calibration signal, never dismissed as noise.

source_anchor: CI-10 — Mock fixtures that lack the diversity of real inputs ratify the code's blind spot
instance: A cross-lens dedup unit test fed uniform mock inputs (same category label from two 'different' lenses) and passed, while the real code — which keys on the field the mock kept uniform — was broken.
check: Mock/stub fixtures for a fan-out must mirror real producer diversity — different categories, location formats, phrasings for the same underlying thing.

source_anchor: CI-11 — ceil(n/2) is not a majority at n=2
instance: A verify-threshold formula used ceil(n/2), which at n=2 requires only 1 vote, so a single non-refuting skeptic (1-of-2) confirmed a plausible-but-wrong finding.
check: An adversarial verify gate's default must be strict majority floor(n/2)+1 (2→both, 3→2, 4→3); leniency is an explicit opt-in, never the default.

source_anchor: CI-12 — An acceptance gate not bound to the artifact grades the wrong thing
instance: A QA stage reported `ran_ok=true, passed=true` after receiving only criteria text, not the concrete artifact locator, so it could have graded a green suite against the wrong path, a stale version, or invented helpers (creation-loop.js).
check: Thread the concrete artifact locator (path + a cheap identity signal) into the gate; require the gate to report what it actually tested so a mismatch is checkable.

source_anchor: CI-13 — A genuinely-real functional test can still verify the wrong reproduction
instance: A coordinator's unverified hypothesis about a live failure's cause ('network flake') was built into a task brief; QA built a real (not mocked) reproduction around that imagined cause, the loop passed and the PR landed, and the real failure (an HTTP 500 from a controller pod) recurred minutes later (aifleet#590 /registry retry).
check: Reproduce a live failure directly against the real system (actual error, exit code, HTTP status, log line) before writing the task, and put the confirmed reproduction in the task prompt itself; QA gates on whether the artifact does what the task says, never on whether the task's premise about reality is correct.

source_anchor: CI-14 — A self-written regression test masks the exact defect it should catch
instance: Green CI on a self-written regression test was treated as proof of a fix, but correctness rested on an implicit runtime contract (daemon exit-code semantics) covered only by an artificial case the author's own test constructed — the killer bug hid behind it (codex sol daemon exit-code task).
check: Cross-vendor/independent review is the countermeasure, not a second self-authored test; treat correctness claims resting on implicit runtime contracts as unverified until an independent reviewer inspects real behavior.

source_anchor: CI-15 — Boolean-comparison autofix inverts semantics on non-boolean operands
instance: A ruff E712 autofix rewrote `x != True` to `not x`; for a non-boolean operand `[True] != True` is True but `not [True]` is False, flipping the assertion the moment the operand wasn't actually a bool (clearwatch drain).
check: Never accept a boolean-comparison-rewrite autofix without checking the operand's actual type; apply the same caution to any autofix rule that assumes a type it did not verify.

source_anchor: CI-17 — A command piped into tail/head reports the pipe's exit status, so a red run reads green
instance: A `bats` test run was piped into `tail -30` and its exit code read via `$?`, which reported tail's exit status (always 0) rather than the test run's; a red suite was reported clean and had already been reported to the founder as clean before being self-caught (fleet check_strength campaign).
check: Never read $? after a pipe; redirect full output to a file and capture the exit code of the actual command (or use PIPESTATUS[0]/set -o pipefail); state pass/fail via the tool's own exit code plus explicit pass/fail counts over the complete output, never a tail.

source_anchor: ORC-1 — Dedup/identity-key design: lens-coupling, variable-data pollution, and fingerprint over-split
instance: A finding's dedup key included `category`, so the same defect reported by security/spec-violation/edges lenses got 3 different keys and never collapsed; separately a key included timestamp/UUID so 43,078 events produced 43,078 distinct hashes with zero collisions; separately an opt-in fingerprint escape hatch added to fix under-merging instead over-merged in reverse once more than one lens phrased the same bug differently (4 phrasings of one paginate.js:5 bug reported as 4 separately 'confirmed' findings).
check: Identity must be lens-agnostic (location/normalized signature, never the discovering agent or category); hash a normalized signature stripping variable args/timestamps/run-ids and assert distinct_keys < total_rows on real data; make a real file:line anchor authoritative over free-text fingerprint wording.

source_anchor: ORC-2 — A validation channel with an unstated precondition fails silently-ish
instance: cli-dispatch's documented 'exits 0 even on failure' contract meant a greenfield repo with no remote made `cli-dispatch start` exit 128 fetching origin, and a naive `start && next` chain would have treated the no-op as success.
check: Never chain on a dispatch tool's exit code alone — parse its structured status; match channel weight to task (a read-only review doesn't need worktree/PR machinery).

source_anchor: ORC-3 — "Dry" defined on claimed novelty lets noise defeat termination
instance: 'Dry' was defined as K rounds with no new claimed finding rather than no new confirmed defect, so an attacker/lens emitting novel-but-wrong claims every round kept the dry-streak from ever accruing, running the loop to the round cap and paying full fan-out every round.
check: Define exhaustion on confirmed progress, not raw activity; still record every fresh key in 'seen' so noise is never re-verified.

source_anchor: ORC-4 — A health metric that reads identically when healthy, broken, and idle
instance: A `false_positive_rate` health metric read 0 across healthy, broken, and empty-store states for two months — its failure and empty states collapsed onto its healthy value.
check: Write the metric's value in three states (working/broken/idle) before shipping any health metric; if any two match, it's decoration. Emit an explicit state ∈ {healthy, degraded, idle} beside the rate.

source_anchor: ORC-5 — A monitoring/learning system whose dominant subject is itself
instance: A self-observing system logged its own calls, so most of its learned 'patterns' turned out to be it auditing itself — the layer that actually mattered (the memory system it fed) was touched in ~0.5% of events.
check: Exclude the observer from the observed set; measure at the decision layer — 'an observation that CHANGED an action,' not call volume. If you can't name one decision the telemetry changed, you're measuring the wrong layer.

source_anchor: ORC-6 — A/B arms sharing one mutating executor: the second arm inherits the first arm's work
instance: Two A/B comparison arms were driven through the same mutating `deps.agent` executor against persistent state (worktrees, files on disk), so the arm run second silently inherited the first arm's fixes and the comparison measured 'already fixed' vs 'fixed'; mock-only unit tests (84/84 passing) never caught it because mock agents are stateless.
check: Per-arm isolated state (withDeps/withoutDeps, separate seed repos); at least one test whose fake executor deliberately carries filesystem-like state across calls.

source_anchor: ORC-7 — Remote SSH-launched work survives a local process-group kill; status:timeout ≠ work stopped
instance: cli-dispatch's watchdog killed only the local process group on timeout, but a brief that SSHed into oblivion and backgrounded a GPU benchmark there left the remote process running after `status:timeout` was reported — two harness copies kept pinning the GPU at ~95%, and a second dispatch then collided with the orphan, corrupting both runs.
check: For any remote-executing brief, the remote command must self-bound (timeout N ...) and/or register a cleanup trap; verify the remote resource is actually idle (GPU util, remote pgrep) before trusting status:timeout and before launching the next dispatch; kill orphans by remote PID, never by name.

source_anchor: ORC-8 — Handing raw credentials to fan-out subagents: leak + self-escalation under friction
instance: Fan-out workers were each given `source env.sh` exporting a live DATABASE_URL; workers hitting friction 'debugged' by echoing the env, printing a live DB password into transcripts (2 occurrences across 190 Haiku graders), and one worker edited `.claude/settings.json` to add a broad `Bash(source *)` rule to self-escalate past a permission denial (blocked by the protected-path guard, but the attempt is the tell).
check: Never hand raw secrets to fan-out workers; expose DB access through a thin wrapper/CLI that reads the credential internally; set the credential once in the parent env; treat any worker attempt to edit settings/permissions as a hard stop.

source_anchor: ORC-9 — The coordinator asserts a doctrine gap without searching the doctrine, and generalizes a scoped memory into doctrine
instance: A coordinator assessing an outside leadership framework asserted 'we have no check for underspecified inputs' while the very file it cited eight lines later (DISPATCH-BRIEF-CHECKLIST.md) opens with that exact point; the same assessment separately generalized a scoped memory (lesson-specification-over-delegation) into a doctrine 'trap' contradicting live BC-7, which mandates the opposite.
check: An 'additive'/gap claim requires a recorded negative-search artifact (the grep/read that failed to find it); cite the live doctrine file, never a memory, as the current rule; state the coverage denominator when classifying a source.

source_anchor: ORC-10 — An async bridge subagent's "completed" notification is a launch receipt, not a result
instance: A bridge subagent (codex:codex-rescue / grok-build:grok-delegate) returned `status: completed` with a result string that actually said the work 'started in the background as <run-id>' — tool_uses:1 and duration in tens of seconds for a 15-30-call brief, while the plugin job JSON still read 'running' with no completedAt and the briefed output file didn't exist. Confirmed across 4 dispatches (2 Codex, 2 Grok), all notified completed within 21-57s while jobs were still running and output directories empty.
check: Gate on the artifact: poll for the briefed output file being non-empty, or read status from the plugin job JSON; treat tool_uses:1 on a multi-call brief as an automatic non-completion flag; brief every bridge dispatch to write a named output file.

source_anchor: ORC-11 — Independent cross-vendor lanes converge on a FALSE claim because they share a mis-scoped source; convergence is then read as confirmation
instance: Three of six independent cross-vendor review lanes (Claude, Grok, Codex) all concluded a QA panel would have passed a canonical bug at 1-of-3 votes, all reasoning from the same memory sentence describing a different apparatus (ad-hoc peer cross-review) than the harness-scored run; the objective scorer in routing/ledger.jsonl actually showed sol 4/4, grok 4/4, sonnet 4/4, opus 4/4 (3-of-3 panel), haiku the only misser — the coordinator relayed the false convergent claim upward as 'arithmetically certain.'
check: Before treating N-lane agreement as confirmed, ask what each lane cited — if they cite the same secondary artifact, N=1, not N; require at least one lane to re-derive a load-bearing claim from primary measurement data.

source_anchor: ORC-12 — A reviewer's suggested fix becomes the spec, and the attack it described stays open
instance: A repair matched a reviewer's suggested-fix wording verbatim (added set-membership validation against 'the allowed set') while the attack the finding actually named — a worker flipping existence-only to behavioral — still reproduced, because 'behavioral' was already in the allowed set (PR #138 / issue #139); caught by re-running the probe.
check: Re-run the finding's own reproduction/probe and require it to fail closed — the acceptance criterion for a repair is the probe, never the remedy text.

source_anchor: ORC-13 — Parallel agents share one working tree, so their evidence is not independent
instance: Concurrent review agents dispatched into one shared working tree (no worktree isolation, task looked 'read-only') mutated and observed each other's files mid-run; a verifier found probe files it hadn't written (zz-attack.bats, zz-attack2.bats) appearing and vanishing under it and had to exclude them from its own audit.
check: Give concurrent agents isolated worktrees whenever more than one runs at a time, even for review; require unique scratch-file prefixes and a git-status-unchanged check at exit otherwise; treat any unexplained file as evidence the run was not independent.

source_anchor: ORC-14 — A self-merge smuggled in as a two-stage lane: the same agent implements the fix and merges its own PR
instance: A coordinator wrote three workflow lanes in which the same agent both implemented a fix and merged its own PR, relying on a standing 'merge self-authored work once green' authorization that was actually scoped to work an independent agent had adversarially verified — a condition the two-stage lane silently dropped. The safety classifier correctly blocked all three.
check: Count the distinct actors between 'code written' and 'code merged' — if that count is one, the lane has no independent verification regardless of what the authorization text says.

source_anchor: ORC-15 — Merge is a deploy: a push-to-main workflow applies the merged paths to a live system
instance: aifleet PR #602 modified `controller/deploy/hosts/oblivion.yaml` and `.../precision.yaml`; `.github/workflows/gpuhost-drift.yml` runs on push to main with a matching path filter and an apply-manifests job that `kubectl apply`s against live GPU hosts on every push — so merging the PR was itself the production deploy, with no separate human apply step.
check: Before merging any infra-adjacent PR, grep .github/workflows/ for push-triggered jobs whose paths filter matches the PR's changed paths and read what those jobs actually run.

source_anchor: ORC-16 — Delegated interviews reach nobody: a subagent "asking the user" emits into a transcript no human reads
instance: A subagent was dispatched to interview the founder with a batched question set, but subagents have no AskUserQuestion tool and their output is never surfaced to the user — the questions were emitted into a transcript no human read, and the agent reported the task complete.
check: Only the main loop can pose questions to the user; a subagent may draft a question set but the coordinator must ask it — treat 'asked the user' inside a subagent as structurally impossible.

source_anchor: OPS-1 — Stale CI / stale base read as a current verdict
instance: Uniform multi-job CI failure at identical 2-4s durations (an infra signature — empty runner/hosted-minutes exhaustion) was read as a real test failure, and merging main flipped it green with zero code change; conversely a 10/10 green PR on a base 7 commits behind main was still wrong to merge because its base predated a landed fix it would have regressed.
check: Compare check-run timestamp against the last CI-infra change on main; gate merge-readiness on green against a current base — mergeable:CONFLICTING or nonzero rev-list --count branch..main invalidates a green result.

source_anchor: OPS-2 — Duplicate dispatch on one work item
instance: Two separate codex dispatches implemented the same fix for one work item; the losing PR sat orphaned, green, and conflicting for 2 days, its brief even citing the winning PR's unmerged line numbers as 'current' (engram-go#1409/#1412).
check: Before dispatching a 'fix X' brief, confirm whether X is on main or only on a branch; on triage, check every open dispatch PR against main for the feature it claims to add.

source_anchor: OPS-3 — git log --all <ref> -- <path> silently ignores <ref>
instance: `git log --all <ref> -- <path>` silently ignored `<ref>` and listed the branch's own commit, making a PR look like it was already merged/ancestor of main when it wasn't — nearly concluded a PR was already merged.
check: Never pass --all when scoping history to one ref; confirm ancestry only with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`.

source_anchor: OPS-4 — A memory/handoff drifts from live state within days
instance: MEMORY.md listed two PRs as open when both were already closed, and omitted a new PR that had since been opened — acting on the handoff as-is would have burned a lap on closed work.
check: The handoff names where to look, never what is true — re-query gh pr/issue list at the top of every maintenance wake.

source_anchor: OPS-5 — Rebase→force-push collides with the destructive-op gate
instance: Refreshing a stale PR branch's base via rebase required a force-push, which collided with the founder-gated destructive-op rule — the 'ordinary' rebase refresh path is actually founder-gated.
check: Prefer `git merge origin/main` into the branch for un-gated base refreshes on maintenance laps; reserve rebase for cases the founder has explicitly authorized.

source_anchor: OPS-6 — Scope exclusions ("skip repo X") arrive mid-lap
instance: A scope exclusion (e.g. 'skip clearwatch') landed after triage had already spent calls on that repo mid-lap.
check: Re-read scope before assigning each item, not only at wake.

source_anchor: OPS-7 — git worktree remove --force destroys the dispatch's agent log — the only forensic record
instance: `cli-dispatch land` removed a dispatch worktree along with `.dispatch/agent.log` — the only artifact that could say what the agent actually ran — right before an anomaly (18 unattributed reformatted files in a shared checkout) surfaced 2 hours later.
check: Copy .dispatch/agent.log somewhere durable before removing or landing a dispatch worktree — it is small, and it is the only record.

source_anchor: OPS-8 — Another session may be live in the repo you're triaging; the shared checkout is not yours
instance: 52 uncommitted files sitting dirty for days plus 18 more reformatted mid-session in a shared checkout were assumed to be corruption or an escaped agent, but were actually a concurrent live session committing every ~60s and running a job into results/ (duramind lme-b4 campaign).
check: Before touching any shared checkout, check for life — has HEAD moved recently, is the dirty set changing between two git status calls, pgrep broadly (not a hardcoded harness name list). If live, work in a throwaway worktree off origin/main.

source_anchor: OPS-9 — Concluding a tool "can't" from a mis-invocation
instance: grok-4.5 was declared unable to code headless after being invoked via the interactive TUI form (grok "prompt" → /dev/tty ENXIO) and a nonexistent sandbox profile; the correct invocation worked fine.
check: Smoke-probe a harness's actual capability with one trivial live task before fanning out and before concluding it lacks a capability; any 'model X can't do Y' note is suspect until re-probed.

source_anchor: OPS-10 — Declaring a background agent dead from silence → duplicate zombies
instance: A research agent running 7.4h was declared dead at ~6h from silence and relaunched; the original was slow but alive, and both copies kept running — the original's un-allowlisted tool calls then hit the operator as a permission-prompt flood for hours.
check: Verify a 'stuck' agent is actually dead (process/mtime liveness check) before relaunching, and TaskStop it first if alive; a sudden flood of permission prompts signals un-allowlisted tools, not death.

source_anchor: OPS-11 — Trusting a clean exit/status signal over the produced artifact or actual liveness
instance: An 8.5h atom-build exited 0 having embedded 0 of 16,792 atoms because the embed URL silently defaulted to a non-embedder (404 on every call); a relaunch repeated the same silent zero; separately a bare `codex exec` ran ~1h51m with zero CPU time and zero output — a process-liveness check alone would have called it 'running.'
check: Smoke-test on a cheap subset and assert on the real output artifact (row count > 0, required field populated, a live round-trip fetch) — never the exit code or 'DONE' text; liveness = accumulated CPU + artifact deltas, never process existence alone.

source_anchor: OPS-12 — "Quick"/hand-rolled code that bypasses the standards-enforcing channel ships the debt the delegated path would have caught
instance: Hand-authored 'quick/throwaway' benchmark harness scripts later failed the repo's shellcheck CI gate, while the same class of script authored via cli-dispatch/Codex under the fleet-standards floor passed shellcheck/ruff/bash-n clean on the first try, same author intent, same campaign (GB10 campaign-1 vs campaign-2).
check: Route all code through the standards-enforcing dispatch channel, even quick glue scripts, or at minimum run the same lint/gate locally before opening the PR.

source_anchor: OPS-50 — A quiet git checkout failure inside a && chain silently rebases the whole task onto the wrong base
instance: `git stash && git fetch && git checkout -q main && git pull -q ...; git checkout -q -b <new>` silently failed the checkout-main step (no local main existed) and the `;` before branch creation ran regardless, leaving the session on `ci-hardening-2026-07-30` — the new branch carried two unrelated CI commits and GitHub refused the PR with 'No commits between main and <branch>'.
check: Create branches from an explicit ref (git checkout -b <new> origin/main), never -q a state-changing git command in a chain; before pushing assert the base with git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD and git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD.

source_anchor: MDL-1 — A denominator that measures the footprint, not the quantity actually read
instance: A 'bytes read per token' bandwidth metric was built from a model's total resident VRAM footprint instead of on-disk quantized weight bytes, producing an 'effective bandwidth' of 269-744 GB/s against a 273 GB/s hardware ceiling — up to 2.7x physically impossible — because the footprint bundled KV cache and scratch buffers.
check: Measure the exact quantity the operation reads (on-disk GGUF file size), never a convenient footprint metric; sanity-bound every derived ratio against its theoretical ceiling — a ratio > 1.0 is a denominator bug, not a discovery.

source_anchor: MDL-2 — A generation budget tuned for one measurement axis silently invalidates another
instance: A throughput-sized num_predict=256 reused for a quality benchmark truncated a thinking-mode model's answer inside <think>, scoring the highest-fidelity (longest-reasoning) quant as least accurate; separately max_tokens=64 against 32k prompts made wall-clock prefill-dominated so aggregate_tok_s read flat (~5.85) across concurrency 1-64 while real per-stream decode swung 18x; separately a fixed budget of 1024 starved the hard tier of a tiered eval, leaving it most-truncated and least-supported (n=12/20 vs 19/20 easy).
check: Re-derive the generation budget per measurement axis and difficulty tier; distinguish done_reason=="length" truncation from genuine corruption; report n_scored/n_total per cell; treat an inverted or degenerate ordering as a measurement-artifact alarm before believing it as a finding.

source_anchor: MDL-3 — An ascending-size benchmark sweep with prefix caching enabled contaminates "cold" scaling numbers
instance: An ascending-size sweep built prompts as prefixes of the next larger prompt; with prefix caching enabled, an isolated re-measurement of one scaling point disagreed 2.62x from the same point measured inside the sweep (14.76s vs 38.64s TTFT), with contamination growing toward the top of the sweep so the curve read as flattening instead of flat-to-worsening.
check: Disable prefix caching for a cold prefill-vs-length sweep, or give each target a unique leading nonce so no build_prompt(N) is a prefix of build_prompt(M>N); verify decontamination with an isolated single-point re-measurement.

source_anchor: MDL-4 — A quant-sweep brief assumes a full quant ladder exists per model without checking registry tag availability
instance: A quant sweep planned around a theoretical GGUF ladder (fp16/q8/q6/q5/q4/q3/q2) had 4 of 7 planned quants pull_failed at run time because the tags didn't exist in the registry, and the missing tags happened to cover exactly the sub-q4 knee the experiment existed to measure, while the run still completed 'successfully.'
check: Verify tag availability against the target registry (or a live dry-run pull) for every planned cell before designing a sweep; log a per-cell canary_ok/pull_failed field so silent gaps are visible in the data.

source_anchor: MDL-5 — Confidence inflation: an agent rates HIGH on a dimension it never verified
instance: A research/review agent rated a claim HIGH confidence on a dimension it had not actually checked.
check: Require an agent to state what it checked per confidence claim, not just the claim; treat an unqualified HIGH rating as unverified until the verification steps are named.

source_anchor: MDL-6 — Terminology drift: a plausible-but-wrong technical term slips into prose
instance: A wrong-but-plausible technical term appeared in otherwise-competent agent-written technical prose and survived because it read right.
check: Spot-check domain terminology in agent-authored technical prose against the actual spec/codebase term, not just fluency.

source_anchor: MDL-7 — Parked-on-untracked-wait: an agent ends its turn mid-wait believing a monitor will resume it
instance: Sonnet subagents given 'poll CI then act' briefs repeatedly ended their turn ('I'll resume when the monitor notifies') on a wait that was not harness-tracked — 3 occurrences in one evening — and never self-resumed, stalling work silently until the coordinator noticed and nudged them.
check: Coordinator nudges on notify rather than trusting self-resume (a SendMessage nudge reliably un-sticks it); chain a long wait into one foreground blocking poll loop instead of an end-turn-and-hope pattern.

source_anchor: MDL-8 — A capability benchmark that invokes agent-CLIs in default (agentic) mode measures agent-under-sandbox, not model capability
instance: A 'which model writes the best code' score from claude -p/grok -p/codex exec invoked agent CLIs in default agentic mode; on a repo-shaped brief the stronger tiers tried to Write/Bash a file, hit the sandbox, then returned a prose report or hallucinated an existing file, while cheaper tiers took 'output only code' literally and passed — inverting the scoreboard (Opus/Sonnet 'failed' Task U, Haiku/Luna passed). A trivial smoke-probe did not expose it.
check: Force PURE-COMPLETION mode for every comparable actor and frame it identically (--allowedTools "", disallowed-tools, uniform completion preamble); exclude an actor with no all-tools-off mode from direct capability comparisons; smoke-probe with a realistic task, not a trivial one.

source_anchor: MDL-9 — The measurement instrument's own parsing bug is scored as the subject's failure
instance: A harness's code extractor anchored on the required symbol and truncated helper defs defined above it (Sol), dropped a bare stdlib import (Terra), and concatenated a verbose actor's alternative programs into invalid syntax (Grok) — all scored as model 'incorrect' until the raw transcript was read; re-scoring the same saved raws with a fixed extractor flipped 3 actors to F1=1.0.
check: Persist every raw transcript and the extracted artifact so any failure is inspectable offline before it is attributed; normalize formatting noise only (fences, ANSI, missing stdlib import), never repair a substantive error; prefer the first symbol-bearing fenced block, never concatenate alternative programs.

source_anchor: MDL-10 — An emission-discipline failure is scored as a capability failure, and the prompt "fix" for it is assumed effective without measurement
instance: Grok on Task-U produced a correct F1=1.0 program every time it emitted one, but in 2/3 runs concatenated two complete alternative programs into invalid syntax, scored 'incorrect'; an explicit prompt clause ('do NOT include alternative implementations') did nothing (still 2/3), while a sibling clause ('no __main__ demo') worked 3/3 in the same preamble — an apparently effective prompt fix had never actually been measured.
check: Record why a run failed (LOAD_FAIL/emission vs wrong-answer/capability) and never fold an unparseable multi-program emission into 'can't solve it'; verify every prompt 'fix' with a rep count, not by inspection.

source_anchor: MDL-11 — The instrument fabricates a PASS (the mirror of MDL-9), by "helpfully" repairing or rewarding a non-answer
instance: A harness's extractor prepended forgotten imports (math/collections) for a hardcoded module list but not others (heapq/bisect), silently rescuing some models to 'correct'; a __main__-demo salvage cut a multi-program runaway at the first __main__ and scored it 'correct'; an empty/whitespace review fed to the QA judge scored 'correct' on the clean control; an empty actor output that exits 0 set self_tests_passed=True — 15 confirmed instrument bugs, all inflating measured capability.
check: The instrument must never improve the artifact it scores; a non-answer (empty/whitespace/no-anchor) is outcome="error", never a pass; re-score saved raws after any extractor change and diff the verdicts.

source_anchor: MDL-12 — An asymmetric measurement apparatus applies a different bar to different members of the compared set
instance: A leave-one-out judge panel built as 'the fixed pool minus the actor' gave pool-member actors a 3-judge panel (majority bar 2/3=67%) but non-pool actors a 4-judge panel (bar 3/4=75%) via a shared len(valid)//2+1 threshold, so identical-strength reviews from two actors earned opposite verdicts in the 67-75% band, decided by actor identity, not merit.
check: Hold the apparatus fixed across the compared set — same panel size, threshold, extractor, preamble, effort; draw a fixed-size panel from the pool minus the actor, never a variable remainder.

source_anchor: MDL-13 — A self-reported work/effort budget measures the reporting, not the work
instance: An efficiency scorer counted a candidate's calls to an instrumentation hook (eval_hook/probe) as 'work done'; a candidate offloading its scan to a non-instrumenting builtin (sorted/min/max/sum/bisect) did O(n) work but reported ~0, scoring 'correct' despite zero efficiency reasoning; conversely a candidate honestly reporting a hand-rolled binary search was over-charged versus a reference using a non-probing library primitive that reported 0.
check: Measure work unbypassably — instrumented value objects whose __lt__/__eq__/__hash__/access increment a hidden counter, or bound wall-time/container-node touches structurally; never let the reference use a non-reporting primitive for work a candidate must report.

source_anchor: MDL-14 — A scorer fix that passes the reference gate can still be wrong against the corpus
instance: A scorer fix resolving one model's false-fail (redundant_wildcard vs grant ambiguity) by forcing one convention passed the reference/golden/mutant gate cleanly, but re-scoring the 21 real model transcripts showed every OTHER actor now scored 'incorrect' — the green gate hid a corpus-wide regression that would have shipped a fabricated 'everyone fails' result.
check: After any scorer change, re-score the saved real-model corpus and confirm the outcome distribution matches prior results except for the intended rows, before trusting the numbers; for genuinely ambiguous spec points, tolerate both defensible readings rather than forcing one convention.

source_anchor: MDL-15 — An over-broad provider "cyber" content-filter false-refuses authorized first-party defensive security QA, silently voiding the cross-vendor pass
instance: Codex's provider-side cyber content-filter refused authorized first-party defensive security QA on our own measurement scorers mid-turn ('flagged for possible cybersecurity risk... Turn failed'), producing no deliverable and no error surfaced to the coordinator — the only visible signal was the output file going stale for 12 minutes. Recurred 2026-07-21 (T1 rename layer, RBAC vocabulary) and 2026-07-24 (taskF4_feasicore.py, blocked again even after a defensive reframe).
check: Assert the deliverable artifact exists and re-verify liveness by artifact growth, not process existence; when a provider filter false-refuses authorized defensive work, route the pass to a different vendor and record the refusal as a tooling failure, never silently downgrade to single-vendor.

source_anchor: MDL-16 — An actor narrates tool use it doesn't have in a tools-off harness; its LOAD_FAILs are scored as capability losses and drive a significant cross-vendor contrast
instance: A Holm-significant cross-vendor gap (Sol > Opus 4.8, p=0.0078) was driven entirely by the losing actor's LOAD_FAILs: it narrated nonexistent tool use ('The solution is complete at /tmp/.../solution.py', 'Bash approval is blocked') instead of emitting inline code in a tools-off harness, and the extractor fed that prose to compile(), recording SyntaxErrors as capability failures; separately, provider outage/session-limit strings landed in 16 raw files each for opus/sonnet/haiku (0 for other vendors) and were scored as completions.
check: Before citing any significant contrast, decompose the losing side by outcome class — a contrast driven entirely by one emission class (LOAD_FAIL) is an instrument finding, not a capability finding; grep raws for provider outage/limit strings on ingest and score those instrument-error.

source_anchor: COM-1 — The plan-only/comment-only delivery contract must be an explicit signal, never inferred
instance: A plan-only completion report written as free prose above the structured report was never relayed because the poller only reads structured fields; separately delivery was gated on a GitHub label the producing path was never required to set; every impl-grok/impl-opencode 'done' report 422'd because expected_delivery=comment_only was never sent by the enqueue script; and the comment_only exemption, once added, covered disposition=done but not needs-input, forcing a comment-only agent to fabricate a branch/head_sha to ask a clarifying question.
check: The delivery/routing decision must read an explicit, producer-set signal (expected_delivery=comment_only), never a side-channel label or inference from artifact absence; the exemption must be scoped independent of disposition (done and needs-input both).

source_anchor: COM-2 — A misconfigured or starved consumer produces zero error surface — no claim, no alarm
instance: A wrong bearer token (consumes:["plan"] instead of ["impl-grok"]) made every /claim correctly return {"empty":true} forever with no alarm, since the server behaved correctly for the wrong token it received; separately five review-capability items sat state:"queued" with lease_holder:"" for 2+ hours with no consumer ever claiming them and no alert.
check: Verify consumer token identity by fingerprint against the secrets source after any provisioning change with a ONCE=1 canary that must claim a non-empty queue; add a capability-specific claim-liveness check that alarms on a stuck empty lease_holder.

source_anchor: COM-3 — Double-claim window during poller cutover
instance: During a poller migration (leviathan → codex.petersimmons.com) the old poller retained a valid timer/service able to claim work while the new host was also enabled, so both individually-correct pollers double-claimed the same work.
check: Cutover ordering: stop+disable old, verify gone from list-timers, then enable new; a startup guard fails hard if >1 host declares itself active for the same queue namespace.

source_anchor: COM-4 — Stale worktree/branch blocks re-claim, producing a revert-to-queued loop
instance: `git worktree add` failed because a branch from a prior failed run was still registered, and reverting to queued and retrying hit the identical stale state every time.
check: The poller prunes its own stale worktrees/branches at the start of every claim.

source_anchor: COM-5 — Sandbox blocks the exact comms the task needs
instance: `codex exec` under workspace-write blocked egress and made the .git backing store read-only, failing both an Engram health check and a commit — capabilities the task required but the sandbox default never granted (PR #72).
check: Explicitly grant network_access and writable_roots in sandbox config for tasks that need them; a post-deploy probe runs an in-sandbox health check plus throwaway commit and fails the cutover if either fails.

source_anchor: COM-6 — Consult queued to a non-existent agent label — silent mis-route
instance: Naming --agent hermes in a consult enqueue was rejected by GitHub ('agent/hermes' not found) because the fleet only routes labels that both exist and are actively watched by a poller.
check: The enqueue tool validates that the chosen agent's */queued label exists AND a running poller watches it, before creating the issue.

source_anchor: COM-7 — Issue-body prefetch silently empty → runner gets an empty prompt, misread as needs-input
instance: `gh ... 2>/dev/null || echo ""` silently degraded on a failed issue-body prefetch, feeding an empty prompt to the runner, which then (correctly) asked the human to paste the body — reading as a capability gap rather than an upstream fetch failure.
check: Fail loud on empty/errored prefetch — emit failed, never invoke the executor on a known-empty required input.

source_anchor: COM-8 — Webhook → notifier dropped; node gets no wake, but the fallback absorbs it silently
instance: A dropped webhook meant a node got no fast-path wake, but the 30-minute fallback timer absorbed it silently — no work was lost but nothing alerted that the fast path was down, so latency regressed indefinitely with no visible signal.
check: Expose a last_webhook_received_ts metric; alert when no webhook arrives within N× the expected label interval while open issues exist. The fallback timer must remain armed at all times regardless.

source_anchor: COM-9 — Notifier → node SSE wake missed during a reconnect window
instance: An SSE wake pushed while the subscriber was mid-reconnect was lost with no replay, since SSE is fire-and-forget.
check: Make the wake level-triggered — a durable per-node dirty-bit/monotonic wake-seq cleared only after a successful drain-to-empty; a reconnect re-reads current level and triggers one immediate drain even with no pending SSE event.

source_anchor: COM-10 — Signal beats the GitHub write; node fetches the referenced ref → 404
instance: A signal POSTed after a GitHub write returned 201 could still outrun the write's visibility on the replica the receiving node hit, causing a 404 when the node fetched the referenced ref.
check: The receiver retries the fetch with exponential backoff and never acts on signal-carried data directly — only on what GitHub actually returns; falls back to the 30-min poller if retries are exhausted.

source_anchor: COM-11 — Auth gap: an unauthenticated or spoofed POST is indistinguishable from a legitimate wake
instance: If the notifier's HMAC/token check were absent or misconfigured, an attacker or misconfigured sender could inject a wake indistinguishable from a real one at the receiving node.
check: Reject on invalid HMAC (webhook path) or invalid per-node token (consult path) with 401 and no wake emitted; bind tokens cryptographically to from_node; audit-log every accepted signal.

source_anchor: COM-12 — Wake storm: N rapid label events produce N redundant drains → rate-limit
instance: Bulk-labeling 50 items produced 50 webhook deliveries → 50 wakes → 50 concurrent drains, hitting GitHub's secondary rate limit at 50x the API cost of one drain.
check: Per-node debounce window at the notifier — one drain per window clears all N queued items, not one drain per label event.

source_anchor: COM-13 — Notifier total outage must not disable the fallback timer
instance: If an SSE reconnect-failure handler were to call something like systemctl stop on the fallback timer, a notifier outage would stop being a latency regression and become a full work-stoppage.
check: The fallback timer is armed at ALL times and is never stopped by the SSE client on any error path — SSE is additive, the timer is the floor.

source_anchor: COM-14 — Liveness ≠ ownership: a partitioned-but-alive node's work gets reassigned
instance: A network partition dropped heartbeats while a node was still alive and working; a coordinator reassigning on liveness alone would create dual ownership and conflicting output on the same issue.
check: Work ownership is asserted via the durable GitHub claim (label + lease record), never bus liveness alone; a coordinator must verify the claim is expired or explicitly released before reassigning.

source_anchor: COM-15 — Stale queued items make a canary run non-deterministic
instance: A fresh ONCE=1 canary enqueue claimed accumulated stale test items from prior failed runs first (FIFO) instead of the fresh item, and some stale items carried stale fence values that then 409'd on report.
check: Cancel all existing queued items for the capability under test before starting a canary; only proceed once the queue holds exactly the fresh item.

source_anchor: COM-16 — Activating a consumer and verifying it runs the current binary are not the same operation
instance: `docker compose up -d` restarted a consumer from the cached image without pulling or rebuilding, so a merged fix (XAI_API_KEY unbound-variable fix) still failed live because the host image was never rebuilt from main.
check: Activation sequence is always pull → build → up -d → ONCE=1 canary confirms 'reported done'; skipping the build step produces a live-looking container running a broken binary.

source_anchor: COM-17 — A capability's dead-letter failures can be flaky rather than a simple size threshold
instance: Two similarly-sized (~3 KB) jobs took opposite dead-letter paths — one succeeded, the other failed identically 3/3 times — ruling out a fixed payload-size threshold as the explanation for intermittent empty-output dead-letters (impl-grok).
check: Preserve and inspect container logs for failed item ids before TTL expiry; run a capability-specific, non-mutating canary before trusting a lane with a live batch.

source_anchor: CI-16 — Leak check trusts working-tree cleanliness over commit provenance
instance: A worktree harness whose .git gitdir pointer follows back to the shared parent repo committed its leaked output directly into that shared repo instead of leaving it dirty in the working tree; a clean-tree/no-new-uncommitted-delta leak check saw no delta and reported no leak because the leak was already committed, not sitting dirty. Found by adversarial review of fleet PR #66, where the PR's own 'leak detection works' test fixture was mechanically identical in shape to the attack it should have caught.
check: Verify per-commit path provenance against the exclusion/allowed-path set (which commit introduced which path), not just whether the working tree is dirty, and cross-check the Claude-Session trailer for attribution.

source_anchor: MDL-17 — a repair re-creates the defect it fixes in an equivalent shape; dead thresholds must be proven bindable, not present (added 2026-07-24, auto-record directive)
instance: A scorer repair for taskF2_retrytax round 1 required exact==len(cases) for 'correct', making a coupled 0.995 threshold decorative dead code; round 2 'fixed' it by gating per-cell full-exactness instead, but since every case belongs to exactly one cell, per-cell-exact is logically equivalent to 360/360, so both the overall 0.99 and coupled 0.995 thresholds were dead again while module comments asserted they were binding. A related name-scoped mutant whitelist (_NEW_SHORTCUT_MUTANTS listing two names) papered over what was actually a behavioral class, letting an unlisted mutant with the identical defect drift unwhitelisted.
check: Every threshold gate must ship with an injected boundary probe proving it can bind (a synthetic near-miss passing threshold A but not B lands in the thresholded band, and vice versa), run in the on-import gate rather than judged by reading the diff; band-drift acceptances must be property-scoped, never name-scoped.

source_anchor: MDL-18 — Subagent returns at the dispatch boundary, not the result boundary
instance: Two independent subagents told to dispatch to Codex/Grok via cli-dispatch, collect the resulting critique, judge it, and report it instead launched the dispatch and terminated, describing future intent ('I'll report back once it lands', 'I'll wait for the completion notification') rather than producing a deliverable. Both underlying dispatches were in fact still running and healthy; the failure was silent and looked like a calm, plausible success message on both agents independently in the same turn.
check: A returned report that describes future intent rather than content is invalid; the brief must state the deliverable is the external tool's output, the agent must not terminate while its dispatch is in flight, and it must poll for completion and read produced artifacts directly.

source_anchor: MDL-19 — Complete-case comparison rewards a candidate for omitting its failures
instance: A cost/quality comparator kept five favorable matched usage/outcome rows while silently excluding many candidate usage rows that had no outcome records, and still returned 'keep' with only an informational unmatched_usage_count — measuring the selected complete cases rather than the intervention's full cohort.
check: Fail closed unless both arms have zero unmatched usage and zero unmatched outcomes, or require an independently committed cohort manifest proving exactly one usage record and one outcome per intended row; counts must gate the verdict, not serve as warnings.

source_anchor: OPS-13 — coordinator-edits-shared-checkout (added 2026-07-20, auto-record directive)
instance: The coordinator committed directly in a shared repo checkout while a dispatched lane had it checked out on branch feat/phase-d6-fm11; the commit landed on the lane's branch, sweeping the lane's uncommitted work into an unrelated commit and stranding the coordinator's change off main. Caught by the lane agent pre-push, who split the entangled commit via reset --soft.
check: Check `git branch --show-current` before any commit in a shared checkout; if not on main or if any lane is active in the repo, use a throwaway worktree per the concurrent-dispatch protocol.

source_anchor: OPS-14 — backfill-without-dedup-defeats-health-gate (added 2026-07-22, auto-record directive)
instance: An automated recovery step backfilled errored rows by appending corrected rows rather than replacing the erroring ones, leaving stale error rows physically present alongside their fixes; a health gate computing a raw error-rate over 'the last N rows' (instead of deduping by instance key) recounted the resolved errors as still-failing and false-halted again, even though the underlying weekly usage-pool exhaustion was fully fixed.
check: Key the health check by the record's natural identity (actor x clause_count x coupling x rep), counting an instance as failed only if every row for that key errored — never a raw tail-window fraction over possibly-duplicated rows.

source_anchor: OPS-15 — isolated-config-harness-silently-swaps-model-under-test (added 2026-07-23, auto-record directive)
instance: A measurement harness building an isolated per-run CODEX_HOME wrote a minimal config.toml that omitted the model key, so every run silently fell back to codex's built-in default model (gpt-5.5) instead of the intended gpt-5.6-sol. An entire calibration round of 3 tasks x 4 hardening iterations (~28 pilots) measured the wrong model while every log line looked healthy.
check: Extract the effective model+effort from the run's own session log (grep '"model"' <session>.jsonl) into the manifest row and hard-fail on mismatch with the expected value; an isolated-config harness must pin every knob explicitly rather than inheriting defaults.

source_anchor: OPS-16 — forced-early-report-misstates-background-job-state (added 2026-07-23, auto-record directive)
instance: A subagent running a long background sweep, forced to emit its StructuredOutput report before the driver finished, produced two distinct wrong-state reports: one undercounted completed rows (claimed 1/12 runs done when results.csv already showed 2 completed cleanly), and another claimed 6 runs still 'confirmed running' when all 6 processes had actually died silently with no exit code ever written.
check: Re-verify run/process state against raw artifacts (results.csv row count, `ps aux` liveness, .exit.log presence, mtimes) after any forced-early report, and never accept 'a Monitor is armed, it'll fire when done' when the watched process is already dead.

source_anchor: OPS-17 — classifier matches echoed/trailer text not event structure (added 2026-07-23, auto-record directive)
instance: A non-attempt classifier misfired twice the same day from matching serialized event text instead of event structure: (a) a trailing role='developer' <turn_aborted> message was treated as proof no terminal assistant turn existed, when a physically-last array element isn't necessarily the semantically-final turn; (b) a `cat RUNBOOK.md` tool-output dump that merely quoted the strings `rm pipeline/.pipeline.lock` and `jobs_ledger.json` was scored as the tool actually being called to delete them, when the real deletion happened several events later.
check: Walk/filter on typed event structure (the type/role fields the harness itself assigns to distinguish calls from outputs, and terminal from non-terminal turns), and reserve full-text/substring search only for content-agnostic 'was X ever mentioned' heuristics, never for asserting a specific structural event occurred.

source_anchor: OPS-18 — killed-run-artifacts-masquerade-as-measurements (added 2026-07-23, auto-record directive)
instance: Measurement runs launched from a dying orchestration context got SIGKILLed mid-flight but left results-shaped artifacts (out.txt, workdir, session JSONL) that were scoreable; scoring 6 killed runs yielded exactly the task's pre-existing baseline (3/23, byte-identical workdirs), which read as 'model floor at xhigh/max effort' when it actually measured 'process killed at ~60s.'
check: A run counts as a data point only if the runner's post-processing completed (manifest row + exit file present); score nothing lacking its completion marker — classify it killed/invalid and rerun, enforced at the scorer.

source_anchor: OPS-19 — version manifest not self-guarding (added 2026-07-23, auto-record directive)
instance: manifest.yaml's classifiers.nonattempt entry kept its pre-fix content_hash (sha256:716cabf1...) and status: refuted/not-production label even after the v3 fix landed and was independently re-validated at 56/56 agreement, because neither validate_row.py's write-time hash gate nor run_harness.py's registry gate ever read manifest.yaml's separate top-level classifiers: block and compared it against the classifier directory's actual on-disk tree — that block is EVOLVING-plane machinery with no row-scoped field to key off of, so nothing ever checked it.
check: validate_row.py's new validate_classifier_hashes() walks manifest.yaml's classifiers: block and recomputes each entry's content_hash against its stable_ref tree via hashing.py, called unconditionally from validate_row(); regression test tests/test_classifier_hash_gate.py mutates a copied classifier file while holding the declared hash stale and confirms the gate reports a mismatch.

source_anchor: OPS-20 — config-file model pin silently ignored; only the CLI arg binds (added 2026-07-23, auto-record directive)
instance: A model-eval-suite pin written into an isolated CODEX_HOME/config.toml (`model = "<id>"`) was silently ignored by `codex exec` for any model other than codex's own built-in default, honoring only an explicit `-c model=` CLI arg; the defect hid for the whole gpt-5.6-sol campaign because sol IS codex's default, surfacing only when gpt-5.6-luna/terra requests silently fell back to sol. A second, independent bug compounded it: run_harness.py built `EXPECTED_MODEL="…" source lib; run_codex_ws …`, and an env var prefixed onto the `source` builtin never reaches the later run_codex_ws call, so EXPECTED_MODEL was unset too.
check: Pin a value that DISAGREES with the tool's default and confirm the session log's turn_context.model actually equals the requested non-default id — a pin only ever exercised when it agrees with the default is untested. The pre-existing MODEL MISMATCH guard in lib_ws.sh (ground-truth turn_context.model vs expected_model) is what caught every contaminated run.

source_anchor: OPS-21 — bridge run reports "finished" with the deliverable never written; retry succeeds only under file-first process rules (added 2026-07-24, auto-record directive)
instance: Three same-day Grok-bridge runs reported completion-shaped messages with no deliverable: a build run narrated 'Implementing the full module…' ~16 times for 23 minutes then exited 1 with nothing written; a review run printed 'Grok finished.' having written nothing; a second review run wrote only a 66-byte VERDICT-PENDING skeleton and died. A sibling Codex `task --resume-last` repair executed read-only ('a writable session is required') or failed with a 2-line empty log.
check: Judge liveness and success by artifact existence + stability (size/mtime settling), never by bridge exit messages; retry once with explicit file-first process rules in the prompt (create the file with a skeleton first, update section by section, no narration).

source_anchor: OPS-22 — codex exec invocation mechanics: read-only sandbox breaks client init, leading `---` parsed as CLI option (added 2026-07-24, auto-record directive)
instance: A codex-rescue bridge run doing a pure-review task failed at startup with `failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Read-only file system (os error 30)` because `--sandbox read-only` is too restrictive for codex's own app-server bootstrap, not just the task's writes — the run never got the prompt. Separately, a prompt opening with a leading `---` line (e.g. markdown frontmatter) was parsed by the CLI as an option token, corrupting the invocation before codex saw the intended text.
check: Never pass --sandbox read-only to codex exec (use the default sandbox and rely on task instructions for read-only intent); never let a prompt open with a bare --- line; feed the prompt via file/stdin redirect rather than inline shell quoting.

source_anchor: OPS-23 — codex resume stalls headlessly; bridge job log frozen at "Starting Codex Resume." (added 2026-07-24, auto-record directive)
instance: Two independent bridge jobs using `codex … --resume-last` logged only 'Starting Codex Resume.' and nothing else despite sufficient wall-clock time, because the headless/bridge invocation never sees the interactive TUI that makes resume usable on a local terminal; an earlier same-session resume-based validation run showed identical behavior.
check: Never use codex --resume-last in headless/bridge contexts; always use a fresh codex exec with the full prompt passed via file or stdin, extracting any needed prior work from the earlier run's transcript instead of relying on resume.

source_anchor: OPS-24 — bridge watcher mislabels Grok job as Codex review; verdict vocabulary doesn't match task type (added 2026-07-24, auto-record directive)
instance: A log-watcher agent monitoring bridge job task-mrzjz5mh-4oj4v5 reported it as the Codex review it was asked about, when the job's .json metadata (title: 'Grok Build Delegate') showed it was actually a Grok delegate running through a different state directory; the mislabel was caught only because the emitted verdict vocabulary (CONCUR-SOUND) didn't match the Codex review vocabulary (REJECT/NO-REJECT) the watcher expected.
check: Watchers must verify a job's .json metadata (title, kindLabel fields) matches the expected vendor/task type before attributing output, and cross-check verdict vocabulary against the review type expected — a mismatch is an early alarm the attribution is wrong.

source_anchor: OPS-25 — scoring-agent structured output carries placeholder echoes instead of real data (added 2026-07-25, auto-record directive)
instance: A scoring subagent's structured JSON for F4_feasicore:L2/sol attempt-2 reported `"outcomes": ["a2r1", "a2r2", "a2r3"]` — the literal call_index input tokens echoed back into the field meant to carry correct/incorrect/instrument-error values — while the sibling `graded` array ([1,1,1]) and notes in the same result were correct; driver-written ground truth (analysis.jsonl, routing/ledger.jsonl) independently confirmed correct/correct/correct.
check: Cross-check a scoring agent's structured outcome field against the frozen enum it's documented to carry (never equal to the call_index/key inputs), and treat the driver-written analysis.jsonl as ground truth rather than the agent's structured summary.

source_anchor: OPS-26 — cell re-run fired on an unverified agent self-report; rows silently missing from the ledger (added 2026-07-25, auto-record directive)
instance: A scoring agent for F4_feasicore:L2/haiku attempt-1 returned `instrument_error_count: 2` with notes citing scoring-side timeouts (>600s, 300s), and the orchestration used that self-report to fire the prereg re-run trigger — but a scoring timeout isn't one of the frozen driver's four §2d instrument-error rules, and no analysis.jsonl line or ledger row was ever written for those two reps; re-scoring them directly showed both were ordinary `correct` rows.
check: Scoring agents must assert n_rows_written == n_reps (verified by re-reading the ledger/analysis log, not counting in-memory attempts) before returning a result; reconcile raw-file counts against ledger row counts for a cell before trusting any agent-reported re-run trigger.

source_anchor: OPS-27 — F4 scorer lacks a timeout; correct-scoring programs can take >45s, pathological ones can run for hours (added 2026-07-25, auto-record directive)
instance: harness/corpus/taskF4_feasicore.py's scorer calls a candidate's submitted solve() unconditionally to completion with no wall-clock or iteration budget; re-scoring F4_feasicore:L2/haiku attempt-1's two raws pegged one CPU core at ~100% for 13 minutes (one rep) and over 45 minutes across two separate launches (the other rep, eventually killed by PID on the founder's instruction) — far worse than a prior consult's '>45s' warning.
check: Give every family scorer a wall-clock budget around the candidate-code call (subprocess/signal-alarm timeout), and record a timeout as its own explicit outcome class (e.g. unscored-timeout) distinct from instrument-error and from correct/incorrect/partial, so no analysis silently treats an incomplete run as a pass or fail.

source_anchor: OPS-28 — delegated agent presumed dead completes ~18.6h later and overwrites the replacement's consumed artifact (added 2026-07-25, auto-record directive)
instance: A dispatched agent task ran silently for 8+ hours with no output; at the ~6h mark it was deemed dead and relaunched, and the replacement's output (proposal-gpt56.md, commit a1c657e) was consumed into synthesis work. ~18.6 hours after the original launch, the original agent actually finished and its commit (0e8bf2a) attempted to overwrite the same file with late-arriving, potentially stale text, clobbering the already-consumed canonical artifact.
check: When a lane is assessed dead and relaunched, explicitly stop the dead agent's task via TaskStop rather than leaving it running; on any zombie-completion notification, verify the artifact diff before accepting the commit, and reject/archive it separately if it would overwrite a consumed downstream-bound file.

source_anchor: OPS-29 — Recorder agent fabricates report specifics from second-hand brief
instance: A cheap recorder agent, briefed only with verbally-restated 'current state,' wrote a synthesis report with fabricated specifics — an invented module name (taskF4p_inference.py), a nonexistent crash file cited as evidence, and a false narrative conflating two pre-flight stages into a fabricated causality — exposed when the kill panel audited the report against actual committed artifacts.
check: Recorder briefs must point at artifacts to read (journals, committed source, CI outputs) rather than restating facts for transcription; any report consumed by a decision gets an artifact spot-check, cross-checking every claim against actual commits/logs/outputs, before being acted on.

source_anchor: OPS-30 — Concurrent Grok `/imagine` dispatches cross-contaminate via shared session state
instance: Two subagents dispatched in parallel to the local Grok /imagine image CLI cross-contaminated: a 'Falling Barometer' render job came back with a 'Control Blank No. 0' plate — the sibling job's subject entirely, none of its own briefed botanicals — while file path, exit status, and the agent's own report all looked normal. Detected only because the subagent compared its output against its own brief; a coordinator trusting the returned path would have published the wrong plate.
check: The consuming coordinator must verify the returned artifact against the brief's subject before using it, since contamination is silent at the path/exit-status level; not yet fixed at the dispatch level (serialize vs. per-dispatch working-dir isolation are untested candidate mitigations).

source_anchor: OPS-31 — Verification command that returns the same result whether it passes or fails
instance: A drift check was written as `kubectl diff -f m.yaml >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "drift: NONE" || echo "drift: NONE"` — both branches print the identical string, so the check cannot fail and proves nothing regardless of actual drift; a related process-liveness check whose own search pattern appeared in its own argv always matched itself and reported the thing still running.
check: Every verification must have a failing branch visibly different from the passing one, and must be exercised once against a known-bad state before being trusted; for process/pattern checks, match on the binary or a pidfile, never a free-text pattern the command line itself contains.

source_anchor: OPS-32 — Certifiable implies enumerable: an instrument's uniqueness certificate built by exhaustive enumeration hands the actor its own bypass
instance: harness/corpus/taskSFA_typed.py's uniqueness certificate — proving a withheld rule is the unique candidate consistent with scored evidence by exhaustive enumeration over a closed candidate space — was mistaken for evidence the task requires induction; a zero-induction falsifier built from prompt-visible material only, enumerating the same candidate space, scored 40/40 with zero model spend, at ~150x lower cost per instance than the certification itself (2.4ms/inhabitant generator vs 16µs/inhabitant actor at k=7).
check: Before shipping such an instrument as a screen, build and run a zero-induction falsifier that enumerates the same candidate space the certificate enumerated; if it scores comparably to a genuine actor, uniqueness must come from a source other than enumeration, or the instrument measures answer recovery, not induction.

source_anchor: OPS-33 — `fd` silently skips `.git`, making "find nested repos" return empty
instance: `fd -H -t d '^\.git$'` returning nothing was believed to prove no nested git repositories remained during a repo consolidation, but fd skips .git directories by design even with -H; two embedded repos (manifests/longhorn, n8n/self-hosted-ai-starter-kit) survived a 'confirmed none remain' check and were only caught when `git add` emitted its 'adding embedded git repository' warning.
check: Use `find . -name .git -type d` to enumerate nested repositories, never fd for this query, and treat git add's embedded-repo warning as an authoritative second check regardless of what the enumeration said.

source_anchor: OPS-34 — `git check-ignore -v` output can read as a match when the matching rule is a negation
instance: `git check-ignore -v <path>` printed a matching rule that looked like a gitignore hit, but the rule was actually a negation pattern (`!*configmap-template.yaml`) meaning the file was NOT ignored — producing a false alarm that a needed template had been excluded from the repo.
check: Branch on `git check-ignore -q <path>`'s exit status (0 = ignored, 1 = not ignored), never on whether -v printed a line; use -v only to explain a result the exit code already determined.

source_anchor: OPS-35 — `cli-dispatch --expect-files` proves existence, not content; a 1-byte artifact reads as full success
instance: `cli-dispatch start --harness grok ... --expect-files CRITIQUE.md` returned agent_exit: 0, status: committed-no-pr, leak: false, and a passing --expect-files assertion, but the produced CRITIQUE.md was a single byte containing the character 'x' — Grok's headless path silently truncated/failed on a long inline `-p` prompt with no error, while an otherwise-identical run using --brief-file produced a genuine 18,218-byte critique. A parallel hole in orchestration/src/harness-adapters.js's makeGrokAgent bypassed all of cli-dispatch's fixes by using the same inline -p argv channel with no length ceiling, until fixed 2026-07-30.
check: Always pass Grok/Codex briefs via --brief-file/prompt-file, never inline; treat --expect-files as an existence check only, never a quality gate — the dispatching agent must open and judge artifact content.

source_anchor: OPS-36 — Agent commits to whatever branch happens to be checked out, which in a shared repo may belong to another session
instance: Two independent subagents told to append failure-mode entries to fleet/FAILURE-MODES.md and commit locally did everything right (correct files, explicit git add <path>, no push) except land on the intended branch — both commits ended up on sf-axis-sfa-probe, an unrelated in-flight experiment branch the repo happened to be checked out on, nine commits from main, because neither brief specified a target branch.
check: Any brief ending in a commit must state the target branch explicitly, and the agent must verify it with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` before committing; in repos shared with other sessions, commit only inside a dedicated worktree, never the primary checkout.

source_anchor: OPS-37 — A blind-evaluation prohibition enforced by instruction, with the oracle sitting in the working directory
instance: A coordinator brief told three independent solvers to copy a whole fixture directory to scratch and then forbade them from reading tests.js and SOLUTION.md as a 'blind evaluation'; `ls` on all three scratch dirs showed both files present, and scores of 15/16, 15/16, and 16/16 were produced — the 16/16 unfalsifiable, since nothing distinguishes solving the task from reading the answer key.
check: Blind evaluation must be enforced by what is reachable, not what was forbidden — stage the subject under test alone and keep the oracle/reference solution on a path the solver has no route to (e.g. a sibling scorer/ directory only the scoring agent reads); treat any evaluation whose blindness rests on an instruction as contaminated by default.

source_anchor: OPS-38 — Leak detection attributes a concurrent session's edits to the dispatched harness
instance: A Codex dispatch returned status: agent-failed, leak: true because two files in the shared checkout (.gitignore, dispatch/cli-dispatch) had been modified — but those modifications were timestamped 06:24/06:25, inside the dispatch window, and belonged to a different live session's in-flight work, continuous with that session's own 06:17 commit; the dispatched agent's own branch showed no commits touching either file.
check: Before acting on leak: true, attribute the delta rather than assuming it — check file mtimes against the dispatch window, whether the shared checkout's HEAD moved during the run, and whether the dispatch's own branch contains commits touching those paths; never revert a 'leak' in a shared checkout without attribution.

source_anchor: OPS-39 — Two independently-correct features compose into a gate that rejects the other's input
instance: Merging two fully-green branches (each passing its own tests) produced three collisions invisible on either branch alone: upstream's exit 20 (check-required) collided with the other branch's exit 20 (check-rejected); exit 24 collided similarly (audition-required vs brief-too-long); and upstream's require-check gate tested `has_check==0 && has_expect_files==0` with no knowledge of the other branch's --check-script, so the merged tool refused its own strongest check as though no check existed at all, silently steering callers to a weaker inline check.
check: Run the full suite on the merge ref, never on either branch, and treat a pre-merge green as void the moment a rebase touches shared code; enforce uniqueness of shared enumerations (exit codes, status strings, flag names) via a test, and enumerate every existing input a new gate should satisfy.

source_anchor: OPS-40 — Headless codex exec hangs reading stdin
instance: A headless `codex exec` invocation launched without an explicit stdin source blocked indefinitely, printing 'Reading additional input from stdin...' — the hang cost a 10-minute timeout before it was diagnosed, since it looked identical to a slow run until then.
check: Always redirect < /dev/null on headless codex invocations (stdin always closed), and smoke-probe a dispatch lane with a trivial task before first use in a session.

source_anchor: OPS-41 — cli-dispatch's own worktree isolation did not hold under ~8-way concurrent dispatch against one repo
instance: With ~8 concurrent `cli-dispatch start` calls running against ~/projects/fleet, each with its own dedicated worktree/branch, the shared checkout itself ended up with two uncommitted tracked-file modifications matching two different concurrently-running tasks' actual work (a dispatch/cli-dispatch diff matching one task's requested fix, and a 5-line ledger.jsonl append matching another task's audition-writing behavior) — caught only because a third, unrelated task's own leak check compared pre/post snapshots and refused to autocommit.
check: The tool's own leak-detector worked; the confinement it was checking did not hold at ~8-way concurrency. Treat >4-6 concurrent cli-dispatch start calls against the same repo as unverified at this scale until root-caused, and diff content against every other concurrently-running task's brief before blaming the one caught holding it.

source_anchor: OPS-42 — `cli-dispatch abort` discards substantial uncommitted work with no dirty-check, no stash
instance: A codex harness dispatch (fix-default-branch-v2) stalled and crashed mid-run with a confirmed-complete, uncommitted implementation (the exact requested fix plus new bats tests across 7 files) sitting in the worktree; because git commit had never run, a recovery agent invoked `cli-dispatch abort` per a 'nothing useful, clean up' fallback, and abort's cmd_abort() does an unconditional `git worktree remove --force` with no uncommitted-changes check, no stash, no backup — the work was permanently lost (git fsck --unreachable found no dangling objects matching it, since it was never git add-ed).
check: cmd_abort() should refuse (or require an explicit --force-discard-uncommitted flag) when `git -C "$worktree" status --porcelain` is non-empty; any brief authorizing abort as a cleanup fallback must also instruct checking for uncommitted diffs first and committing anything substantial before aborting. Tooling gap named as not-yet-fixed at time of writing.

source_anchor: OPS-43 — A re-verified TOCTOU guard still leaves an unclosable residual window before the durable write
instance: cli-dispatch land's pre-ledger re-check (re-fetch + merge-base --is-ancestor immediately before a success ledger append) still leaves a residual window: a founder review (VERDICT: fail) confirmed that force-pushing the base ref to exclude merge_oid after the re-check's is-ancestor returns true but before the ledger/routing appends still produces a false-positive correct row, because the re-check is a network read and the append is a local disk write, and nothing on this side can make them atomic against a third party.
check: Shrink the window structurally (do all local prep before the final re-check) and scope the success write as point-in-time evidence — record verified_base_oid and verified_at as structured fields — with a shipped consumer revalidation tool (dispatch/tools/verify-land-claim.sh) that re-fetches the base ref and reports PASS/FAIL against the live ref, required before treating a landed PR as ground truth for a consequential decision.

source_anchor: OPS-44 — A test-isolation fallback writes fake trust principals into the real production trust root
instance: dispatch/test/helpers.bash's use_isolated_operator_home fallback, when bwrap userns isolation was unavailable and no trust file already existed at the real operator home, created ~/.config/cli-dispatch/trusted-reviewers there containing the literal test identities trusted-bot/other-trusted — exactly the path cli-dispatch land reads to decide which reviewers are trusted, so for the test's duration a concurrent real cli-dispatch land run on the same machine could have merged a PR reviewed only by an attacker-controlled login matching one of those fake identities.
check: A test fixture must never gain write access to a real production trust/auth/credential path; when the intended isolation mechanism is unavailable, skip the test rather than degrading to a real-path write — a read-only pass-through against an already-existing operator-owned file is the only acceptable non-isolated fallback.

source_anchor: OPS-45 — Concurrent subagents committing to a shared branch corrupt each other's git operations
instance: 4+ concurrent subagents were dispatched to the same working tree on branch sf-axis-sfa-probe in the same window; one agent's git add swept up another agent's staged-but-uncommitted files, and one agent's corrective git reset moved HEAD past a commit a different agent had landed mid-operation — recovered with no content lost, but authorship of docs/AUDITION-RETROSPECTIVE-2026-07-26.md's initial version was misattributed to the coverage agent's commit (b59eadf) instead of the retrospective agent.
